rules.title: Noun and Adjective Gender
rules.title_es: Género del sustantivo y del adjetivo
rules.title_pt: Gênero do substantivo e do adjetivo
rules.explanation: Portuguese nouns and adjectives are **masculine** or **feminine**. Masculine words often end in **-o** (alun**o**) and feminine in **-a** (alun**a**). The article agrees too, **o** aluno / **a** aluna, and so does the adjective, o menino alt**o** / a menina alt**a**.
noticing_prompts: Look at aluno and aluna. Which ending is masculine and which is feminine?
How does the article change between o aluno and a aluna?
The adjective simpático becomes simpática. What makes it change?

structured_input.question: Why does the adjective appear as alta and not alto?
options: It agrees with the feminine noun menina
structured_input.feedback: The adjective agrees in gender with the noun, menina (feminine) takes alta.

structured_input.question: Which is true for you? Choose one.
structured_input.feedback: irmão is masculine and irmã feminine, the ending marks the gender.

quiz.feedback_why: A feminine subject takes the feminine form aluna and the article a.
The masculine noun menino takes the masculine adjective alto.

communicative_production.prompt: Describe a man and a woman you know, with an adjective that agrees with each.
communicative_production.model: Meu amigo é alto e minha amiga é alta.
communicative_production.model_translation: My male friend is tall and my female friend is tall.
communicative_production.hint: Masculine ends in -o, feminine in -a, and the article and adjective agree.

rules.title: Forms of Address (tu, você, o senhor)
rules.title_en: Forms of Address (tu, você, o senhor)
rules.title_es: Formas de tratamiento (tu, você, o senhor)
rules.title_pt: Formas de tratamento (tu, você, o senhor)
rules.explanation: Portuguese has three ways to say **you**. **tu** is informal (friends, family) and takes the 2nd person verb, tu fala**s**. **você** is the neutral, everyday form and takes the 3rd person, você fal**a**. **o senhor / a senhora** is formal (respect, elders, strangers) and also takes the 3rd person, o senhor fal**a**.
noticing_prompts: Compare tu falas and o senhor fala. Which verb ending goes with tu?
você and o senhor use the same verb form. Which person is it?
When would you choose o senhor instead of tu?

structured_input.question: Why is it pode and not podes?
structured_input.feedback: você, like o senhor, uses the 3rd person, so você pode.

structured_input.question: How would you speak to YOUR teacher? Choose what fits.
structured_input.feedback: With a teacher many speakers use o senhor or a senhora (formal) or você (neutral), tu is informal.

quiz.feedback_why: tu takes the 2nd person form falas.
o senhor takes the 3rd person form pode.

communicative_production.prompt: Ask if someone has time, once to a friend (tu) and once to a stranger (o senhor).
communicative_production.model: Tu tens tempo? O senhor tem tempo?
communicative_production.model_translation: Do you have time? Do you have time?
communicative_production.hint: tu takes the 2nd person (tens), o senhor takes the 3rd person (tem).

rules.title: Ser vs Estar
rules.explanation: Both **ser** and **estar** mean **to be**. **ser** is for permanent, defining facts (origin, profession, identity), Eu **sou** do Brasil. **estar** is for temporary states and locations, Eu **estou** cansado, A porta **está** aberta.
noticing_prompts: sou professor and estou cansada, which one is a lasting fact about the person?
é grande and está fechada, which one describes a temporary situation?
Which verb would you use for I am in Brazil right now?

structured_input.question: Why está and not é?
options: Being open is a temporary, changeable state
It is a permanent trait of the door
é is only used for people
structured_input.feedback: A changeable state or condition takes estar, so está aberta.

structured_input.question: What is true about you right now? Choose one.
structured_input.feedback: All three use estar for a temporary state or a location.

quiz.feedback_why: Origin is a permanent fact, so ser gives sou.
A temporary state takes estar, so estamos.

communicative_production.prompt: Say one permanent thing (ser) and one temporary thing (estar) about yourself.
communicative_production.model: Sou estudante e estou feliz hoje.
communicative_production.model_translation: I am a student and I am happy today.
communicative_production.hint: Use ser for identity and traits, estar for states and location.
